message.content:
**The Kiss** by Auguste Rodin (1889) is widely regarded as the most iconic and celebrated sculpture of the 19th century. ### Why it stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading French sculptor who bridged the 19th and 20th centuries | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist – a naturalistic portrayal of a couple in an intimate embrace | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and human intimacy.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its expressive surface and dynamic composition exemplified Rodin’s mastery of form and texture. | | **Legacy** | • Frequently reproduced in bronze, marble, and other media.
• Continues to be referenced in popular culture, literature, and film.
• Its fame helped cement Rodin’s reputation as the preeminent sculptor of his era. | While other 19th‑century masterpieces—such as **The Gates of Hell** (unfinished, 1880‑1908) or **The Statue of Liberty** (1886)—are also monumental, **The Kiss** remains the most instantly recognizable and frequently cited example of 19th‑century sculpture.
